newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia bourse plumbs all-time low as Dadas sinks.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia bourse plumbs all-time low as Dadas sinks.

text.p: Slovenian shares careered to an all-time low on Tuesday as market heavyweight Dadas was suspended from trading after its share price went into a freefall of over 50 percent on Monday.

"Trading in Dadas was suspended because of the deep fall on Monday. Trading will resume after the company explains whether there were any changes in its business that had initiated the fall," bourse spokeswoman Lidija Gabrijelcic said.
Dadas fell 53 percent on Monday as investors bailed out of the financial consultancy on rumours its broking unit may be banned from trading, while the group itself may face bankruptcy.

"The fall was initiated by virtually no demand for Dadas, while many investors wanted to get rid of its shares on the belief Dadas might eventually face bankruptcy," said Sergej Racman, a trader of brokerage PM&A.
"There're several indicators that show Dadas is facing liquidity problems and would not be able to meet obligations to its creditors," he added.

The stock market's watchdog in March started procedures to ban Dadas' mutual fund Proficia Dadas and its broking arm from trading, claiming they were rigging prices by trading among its affiliated companies.
Since then Dadas has shed 95 percent, sent the benchmark index down over 42 percent while dealing the country's fledgling stock market a heavy blow in its attempts to attract more foreign capital.

Dadas liquidated Proficia Dadas in July. The fund, which used to manage around six billion tolars ($44.6 million) of capital from some 3,500 investors, told investors it would return their money in stages within the next four years.
"It's becoming more and more clear that Dadas will not be able to return that money and will therefore sooner or later go bankrupt," said Borut Stariha, a trader of brokerage Alpoma.
He said Dadas shares could continue their downward trek when trading resumes, possibly at the end of the week.

The share price hit a peak of 390,000 tolars on August 26, 1993. On Monday, it stood at just 12,811 tolars. The blue-chip SBI index was down 0.19 percent at 891.93 to record a new life low after plunging five percent on Monday.
Dadas said it had no idea why its share price collapsed.
"There were no changes in the company that could have initiated the fall," spokesman Andrej Rakovic told Reuters without elaborating. ($ = 134.6 Slovenian Tolars)
